levels.how: Levels are the rubric's fit bands (1 Very low, 2 Low from 40, 3 Moderate from 55, 4 Good from 70, 5 Strong from 85), taken from the best fit across your roles (the page's best match), so any role can carry you to the next level. The smallest set is the fewest open actions whose expected effects (each weighted by its chance, within the projection caps) take that best fit to the next level; the date assumes they land on their target dates, and lifted_role is the role that then holds the best fit. quests is the dashboard's one ranked list of actions (Do next, the quests, the badges and the plan list all follow it): the actions on the path to the next level first (the smallest set, or when none reaches it on expected odds, the best-case set), in target date order, then the rest by points per hour. Every action shows one points number on the page, points_expected: what that action alone adds to the best fit toward the next level, chance weighted and within the caps, counted on lifted_role, with on_best_role_today when that differs. Actions that raise the same factor overlap, so quest points do not simply add up. Only the What if rail shows another number, what an action adds with everything else switched on. Nothing here is made up: it all comes from the runs and the plan.

strengths.text: Ten years running warehouse and transport operations and programs.
A verified open-source evaluation tool with 14 releases and outside contributors.
Full work rights in Australia and New Zealand, where Initech and Acme hire.

weaknesses.text: No warm path into Initech Robotics yet.
No product management title, so product roles see a hard-requirement gap.
The LinkedIn headline overstates team size (40, when the evidence says 8).
Nothing built specifically for Acme AI yet.

opportunities.text: Initech Robotics has program and product roles open in Melbourne and Brisbane.
Globex Labs lists an AI Success role in Singapore that names logistics customers as a plus.
Acme AI runs a public evaluation challenge every quarter.

threats.text: Government-facing roles at Acme AI need US citizenship and a clearance.
Recruiters compare public profiles with resumes at screening; a mismatch reads as dishonest.
Product roles ask for 5 or more years with a product title.

strategies.text: Use ten years of warehouse programs to go after Initech's fleet deployments role in Melbourne.
Use route-eval and the logistics background to stand out for Globex's AI Success role.
Lean on Australian work rights and focus on Australian roles, not US government ones.
Fix the missing warm path into Initech to unlock its open roles in Australia.

Correct the overstated team size before any recruiter compares it with the resume.
Do not spend effort on product roles that ask for years of product titles; keep them in the backlog.
